summary: The open gap asks whether the off-main-thread fast path ever produces a harmful outcome. Rather than hunt for a race window that may not be winnable, this turn targets a facet of the same handler that is deterministic and that my earlier reasoning walked past: processHeartbeat checks the node's shutdown channel first and returns without responding when it is closed, while the transport that dispatched the request waits on the response channel it supplied. The state that exposes this is ordinary rather than exotic - a caller that shuts the node down without waiting on the shutdown future leaves the transport open, and it is the node's own shutdown future that closes it. So the new harness builds the same single node over the same fast-path transport, delivers one heartbeat while the node is live as a control, then shuts the node down without closing the transport and delivers a second heartbeat one term above the node's current term, recording whether a response ever arrives inside a bounded interval and whether the term moved. That term operand is what makes the outcome interpretable rather than merely timed: if the handler returned at its shutdown check then no term logic ran and the term stays put, while a response plus a term movement would mean the handler ran normally and the suspicion is defeated. I registered the question as a gap on the same investigation rather than opening a new one, since it is the same handler and the same responsibility, and I assert nothing about the outcome until the receipt exists. The harness file was rewritten for this case and validates; the earlier harnesses are retained in their fixed experiments, and the four witnessed findings plus the unresolved threading claim remain recorded and unaffected.
